content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors propose OGNN which includes the ego node feature, the aggregated node feature and the graph structure feature to generalize well to the whole spectrum of homophily.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength
The experiments on graphs with different homophily levels are comprehensive

## Weaknesses
1. The writing needs to be improved.
2. Some experiments and comparisons are missing.
3. More analysis is needed


## Questions and Comments

1. Why do you identify the three aspects “ego node feature, aggregated node feature, and graph structure feature” instead of other aspects?

2. Why do you want to train your model with a bi-level optimization framework? Did you train other baselines with bi-level optimization as well?

3.  OGNN is a combination of H2GCN and LINKX, what are the advantages and contributions in OGNN.

4. The claims made in this paper about the 3 aspects lack analysis and theoretical verification.

5. What is the performance of OGNN on the 6 benchmark datasets Squirrel, Chameleon, Film, Cornell, Wisconsin and Texas [1]

6. Some recent works find some empirical and theoretical  evidence that heterophily is not always harmful and homophily is not always necessary for GNNs [2,3]. How.does this work align with the previous works.

7. Some missing comparison, e.g. BernNet [4], ACM-GCN [3] and GloGNN[5].

[1] Pei H, Wei B, Chang K C C, et al. Geom-gcn: Geometric graph convolutional networks[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2002.05287, 2020.

[2] Ma Y, Liu X, Shah N, et al. Is homophily a necessity for graph neural networks?[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.06134, 2021.

[3] Luan S, Hua C, Lu Q, et al. Is Heterophily A Real Nightmare For Graph Neural Networks To Do Node Classification?[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2109.05641, 2021.

[4]  He M, Wei Z, Xu H. Bernnet: Learning arbitrary graph spectral filters via bernstein approximation[J]. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 2021, 34: 14239-14251.

[5] Li X, Zhu R, Cheng Y, et al. Finding Global Homophily in Graph Neural Networks When Meeting Heterophily[J]. arXiv preprint arXiv:2205.07308, 2022.

content.summary_of_the_paper: GNNs tend to underperform in the presence of heterophilic graphs. Improving GNN for heterophilic graphs is an important problem. This paper proposes a new model for learning on heterophilic graphs. The new model fuses three different features 1] Ego Features 2] Neighborhood Aggregation Features and 3] Graph Structural Features. Additionally, the fusion parameters are treated as hyper-parameters and tuned over the validation set using bi-level optimization. The paper reports gains on several datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
# Strength:
1. The paper is clearly written and easy to read.
2. The reported results shows that the proposed approach gets marginal gains over SoTA models.
***
# Weaknesses:
1. The proposed approach is not very novel. The proposed approach can be seen as two GPRGNN models built using two different reference operators - normalized adjacency and adjacency matrices and then fused together. It is unclear as to why such a combination would do well.
2. Few newer models are missing from comparison [A, B]
3. The performance numbers for GPRGNN on Citeseer reported in [A] or the more recent paper [C] do not quite match with what is reported in this paper. It would be good to verify these discrepancies.
***
# References:
- [A] BernNet: Learning Arbitrary Graph Spectral Filters via Bernstein Approximation, Mingguo He, Zhewei Wei, Zengfeng Huang, Hongteng Xu, NeuRIPS 2021.
- [B] AdaGNN: Graph Neural Networks with Adaptive Frequency Response Filter, Yushun Dong, Kaize Ding, Brian Jalaian, Shuiwang Ji, Jundong Li, CIKM 2021.
- [C] A Piece-wise Polynomial Filtering Approach for Graph Neural Networks, Vijay Lingam, Manan Sharma, Chanakya Ekbote, Rahul Ragesh, Arun Iyer, Sundararajan Sellamanickam, ECML PKDD 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well-written and clear to understand. The work is limited in its novelty as it can be see as two GPRGNN models with two different reference operators fused together. Also, it is not clear why this fusion method will give improved performance or at least where the improvements are coming from. The experiment results are missing some of the more newer filter models. Also the performance numbers reported in the paper do not quite match with some of the numbers reported in the prior work. It would be good to thoroughly revisit the experiments and confirm the numbers. The method is reasonably well explained and hence should be easy to reproduce. Also, the paper seems to be promising to share the code in an online repository.
content.summary_of_the_review:
The paper is proposing a new model which will be robust to heterophily or homophily of the graphs. The main contribution of the proposed approach is to use three different features - Ego, Neighbor Aggregation and Structural and combine them. The novelty of the proposed approach is limited as the proposed approach can be reduced to a fusion of two GPRGNN models with two difference reference operators. There is no clear justification of why such a fusion will give improvement in performance. The experimental section needs comparison with few more newer models. Also, the reported numbers do not quite match with what is known in prior works.

Thereby, I am inclined to reject the paper.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes a new model, Omnipotent Graph Neural Network (OGNN), which takes a weighted combination of three types of features to make predictions. The three types of features are adapted from the design elements of several existing methods. The weights are essentially obtained through hyperparameter search on validation set. The proposed model shows SOTA performance on both homophily and heterophily datasets.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strength

1) This paper is clearly-written and easy to follow.

2) The experiments are well-documented and seem easy to reproduce.

## Weaknesses

1) The technical novelty is limited. The three types of features, ego features, aggregated features, and graph structure features are respectively common design components of GNNs and LINK/LINKX. The so-called bi-level optimization is equivalent to a hyper-parameter search on the validation set. 

2) I believe the proposed method is no much different from the following simple baseline: 1) train GCN, H2GCN, GPR-GCN, and LINKX separately; 2) have a weighted ensemble of the four models with the weights searched on the validation set. I would imagine both the performance and the training costs would be very similar to the proposed OGNN. The empirical improvements would be very marginal if compared to this simple ensemble baseline. The "average rank" metric is misleading. 

3) In fact, I find the goal of searching for a whole-spectrum model is not well-justified in the first place, given that there could be a simple ensemble solution.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: This paper is overall clearly-written and seems reproducible. The novelty is rather limited.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I find the goal of this work (finding a whole-spectrum model over various levels of homophily) is questionable. The proposed method is no much different from an ensemble of existing baselines and the empirical improvements are marginal.

content.title: Break the Wall Between Homophily and Heterophily for Graph Representation Learning
content.TL;DR: This work proposes a new GNN model called OGNN (Omnipotent Graph Neural Network) that extracts different aspects of graph representations to generalize well on the whole spectrum of homophily.
content.abstract: Homophily and heterophily are intrinsic properties of graphs that describe whether two linked nodes share similar properties. Although many Graph Neural Network (GNN) models have been proposed, it remains unclear how to design a model so that it can generalize well to the whole spectrum of homophily. This work addresses the challenge by identifying three graph features, including the ego node feature, the aggregated node feature, and the graph structure feature, that are essential for graph representation learning. It further proposes a new GNN model called OGNN (Omnipotent Graph Neural Network) that extracts all three graph features and adaptively fuses them to achieve generalizability across the whole spectrum of homophily. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real datasets demonstrate the superiority (average rank 1.56) of our OGNN compared with state-of-the-art methods. Our code will be available at https://*.
